This chapter covers the extensions used in this tutorial.
Most extensions are installed once per project with `quarto add <name>` — the files land in `_extensions/` and should be committed to git.

| Extension | What it adds | Install |
|---|---|---|
| [quizdown](#quizdown-interactive-quizzes) | Multiple-choice, multi-select and ordering quizzes | `quarto add parmsam/quizdown` |
| [Pyodide](#pyodide-live-python-in-the-browser) | Editable Python cells that run in the browser | `quarto add coatless-quarto/pyodide` |
| [pyodide-interaktiv](#pyodide-interaktiv-the-fork-this-tutorial-runs-on) | Same cells, but in a Web Worker — `input()`, animations, Stop, AI feedback | copy the folder (not published yet) |
| [py-exercise](#py-exercise-editable-exercises-with-hidden-tests) | Coding exercises with hidden `assert` tests | copy the folder (not published yet) |
| [math-exercise](#math-exercise-symbolic-answers-checked-with-sympy) | Symbolic maths answers checked with SymPy | copy the folder (not published yet) |
| [JSXGraph](#jsxgraph-interactive-mathematical-graphs) | Interactive mathematical graphs | `quarto add jsxgraph/jsxgraph` |

Extensions can be enabled **globally** in `_quarto.yml` or **per page** in the frontmatter:

```{.yaml filename="_quarto.yml — global"}
filters:
  - parmsam/quizdown
  - coatless-quarto/pyodide
```

```{.yaml filename="page.qmd — per page"}
---
filters:
  - parmsam/quizdown
---
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Filter order matters
Filters run in the order you list them. If a Pyodide extension is on the page, it has to come **before** `py-exercise` and `math-exercise` so those two can reuse its runtime instead of loading a second one.
:::

---

## quizdown — interactive quizzes

**Install:** `quarto add parmsam/quizdown`  
**Source:** [@quizdown] — [github.com/parmsam/quarto-quizdown](https://github.com/parmsam/quarto-quizdown)

:::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}  
```{quizdown}
# Which file controls global project settings in Quarto?

1. [x] `_quarto.yml`
1. [ ] `index.qmd`
1. [ ] `styles.css`

# Select all valid Quarto output formats.

- [x] HTML
- [x] PDF
- [x] Word (.docx)
- [ ] Excel (.xlsx)

# Put the Quarto render pipeline in the correct order.

1. Parse `.qmd` source
2. Execute code chunks
3. Convert Markdown to HTML/PDF
4. Apply theme and styles
```

::::

:::: {.content-hidden when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-note}
## Interactive quiz — HTML only
This quiz requires HTML output. Render as HTML to try it.
:::
::::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Settings

Global quiz settings go inside a `---` block at the top of the quiz:

````{.markdown}
```{quizdown}
---
shuffleAnswers: true    # default: true — randomise answer order
shuffleQuestions: false # default: false — randomise question order
---
```
````

::: {.callout-tip}
`shuffleAnswers: true` is the **default** — answers are shuffled unless you explicitly set it to `false`.
:::

## Question types

**Single choice** — exactly one correct answer:
````{.markdown}
```{quizdown}
# What is 2 + 2?
1. [ ] 3
1. [x] 4
1. [ ] 5
```
````

**Multiple choice** — more than one correct answer:
````{.markdown}
```{quizdown}
# Which of these are programming languages?
- [x] Python
- [ ] Quarto
- [x] R
- [x] JavaScript
```
````

**Ordering** — put these items in the correct order:
````{.markdown}
```{quizdown}
# Put the Quarto render pipeline in the correct order.

1. Parse `.qmd` source
2. Execute code chunks
3. Convert Markdown to HTML/PDF
4. Apply theme and styles
```
````

## Images & code

Include an image in a question:
````{.markdown}
```{quizdown}
# What does this logo belong to?
![](https://quarto.org/quarto.png)
1. [x] Quarto
1. [ ] RMarkdown
```
````

Include inline code in answers:
````{.markdown}
```{quizdown}
# Which chunk option hides the source code?
1. [x] `echo: false`
1. [ ] `eval: false`
1. [ ] `output: false`
```
````

:::

## Pyodide — live Python in the browser

**Install:** `quarto add coatless-quarto/pyodide`  
**Source:** [@pyodide] — [github.com/coatless-quarto/pyodide](https://github.com/coatless-quarto/pyodide)

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Example

:::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```{pyodide-python}
# Edit this code and click Run
words = ["Quarto", "is", "great"]
print(" ".join(words))
```
::::

:::: {.content-hidden when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-note}
## Interactive code cell — HTML only
This live Python cell runs in the browser via Pyodide. Render as HTML to try it.
:::
::::

## Setup & options

Enable per page:
```{.yaml}
---
filters:
  - coatless-quarto/pyodide
---
```

Or globally in `_quarto.yml` (applies to all pages):
```{.yaml}
filters:
  - coatless-quarto/pyodide
```

Per-chunk options:
````{.markdown}
```{pyodide-python}
#| autorun: true     # run automatically on page load
#| read-only: true   # reader cannot edit the code
print("Auto-runs, cannot be changed.")
```
````

## vs. regular Python

| | `{python}` | `{pyodide-python}` |
|---|---|---|
| Runs at | Render time | Read time (in browser) |
| Reader can edit | No | Yes |
| Needs Python installed | Yes (author) | No (reader) |
| Output baked into HTML | Yes | No — computed live |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Package availability
Pyodide runs in WebAssembly. Most pure-Python packages work (`numpy`, `pandas`, `matplotlib`) but packages with C extensions may not be available.
:::

:::

### pyodide-interaktiv — the fork this tutorial runs on

**Install:** copy the folder — not published yet (see the *Install* tab)\
**Source:** [@pyodide-interaktiv] — [github.com/Erasmus-CTM/Pyodide-interaktiv](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/Pyodide-interaktiv)

`pyodide-interaktiv` is a rework of `coatless-quarto/pyodide` that runs Python in a **Web Worker** instead of on the browser's main thread. The cell syntax is identical — `{pyodide-python}` with the same `#|` options — so pages swap between the two by changing one line in `filters:`. What the worker buys you is everything below.

::: {.callout-note}
## The cells on this page use the fork
Every `{pyodide-python}` example on this page — including the one above — is executed by `pyodide-interaktiv`, because only one Pyodide extension can be active per page.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## What's new

| | `coatless-quarto/pyodide` | `pyodide-interaktiv` |
|---|---|---|
| Python runs on | Main thread | Web Worker |
| Page during a long run | Frozen | Stays responsive |
| Runaway loop (`while True:`) | Tab is stuck | **Stop** button cancels it |
| `input()` | Not supported | Real, blocking `input()` |
| Animations | Static image | Interactive player |
| AI feedback | — | Feedback button on every cell |
| Interface language | English | `en`, `de`, `sv`, `no`/`nb`, `da` |

The language is read from Quarto's own `lang:` key, so a multilingual project needs no extra setting — see [Multilanguage Projects](exp_multilanguage.qmd).

## Shared state

All cells on a page share **one** Python session — this is true of the base extension as well — so a later cell can reuse anything an earlier one defined:

:::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```{pyodide-python}
tutorial = "Quarto"
values = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]
print("defined tutorial and values")
```

```{pyodide-python}
# 'tutorial' and 'values' still exist from the cell above
print(f"{tutorial}: sum = {sum(values)}, max = {max(values)}")
```
::::

:::: {.content-hidden when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-note}
## Interactive code cells — HTML only
These live Python cells run in the browser. Render as HTML to try them.
:::
::::

Cells that should run before the reader touches anything use `context: setup`; cells whose result is shown but whose code is hidden use `context: output`.

## `input()`

A cell can stop and wait for typed input without freezing the page:

:::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```{pyodide-python}
name = input("What's your name? ")
print(f"Hello, {name}!")
```
::::

:::: {.content-hidden when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-note}
## Interactive code cell — HTML only
This cell asks for input in the browser. Render as HTML to try it.
:::
::::

::: {.callout-warning}
## `input()` needs cross-origin isolation
Blocking input relies on `SharedArrayBuffer`, which browsers only hand out to cross-origin-isolated pages. A service worker shipped with the extension sets the required headers automatically on your own domain. Learning platforms such as Moodle usually block service workers — there `input()` is simply unavailable and the page says so. Everything else keeps working.
:::

## Plots & animation

With the pyodide-interaktiv extension Animations become plotable.

```{pyodide-python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.animation as animation
import numpy as np

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 100)
line, = ax.plot(x, np.sin(x))

def update(frame):
    line.set_ydata(np.sin(x + frame / 10))
    return line,

ani = animation.FuncAnimation(fig, update, frames=60, blit=True, interval=33)
plt.show()
```

A live version of this is on the [Code page](../../beg/Qmd Files/Example Page/ep_code.html) of the Example Page.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Speed is `interval`, not `frames`
`interval` is the delay between frames in milliseconds — 33 ms is roughly 30 fps. Matplotlib's default of 200 ms looks visibly choppy. `frames` only sets how many frames are drawn, so raising it makes the animation *longer*, not smoother. Every frame is pre-rendered and embedded, so long animations cost render time and page weight.
:::

For special cases, `zeige_animation(ani, format="gif")` and `zeige_animation(ani, fps=30)` control format and frame rate directly.

## AI feedback

Every interactive cell gets a **Feedback** button that sends the current code plus its output to a language model and shows the answer under the cell. A ⚙ icon at the top of the document opens the settings panel:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Provider template | fills in base URL and an example model for OpenRouter, Cerebras, Groq, OpenAI or Ollama |
| Base URL | API endpoint, e.g. `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` |
| API key | stays in the browser only, never in the rendered page |
| Model | free text; **Fetch models** lists the provider's models, free ones by default |
| Feedback mode | **Direct API** or **Copy prompt** |
| Storage | `localStorage` (persistent) or `sessionStorage` (per tab) |

Without an API key, **Copy prompt** mode produces a ready-to-paste prompt for ChatGPT, Claude and the like — no account needed for the reader.

Hints get more concrete with each click on the same cell (1 = nudge, 2 = names the problem, 3 = describes the solution in words — never finished code). Turn it off with `feedback-hints: false`.

```{.yaml filename="page.qmd"}
pyodide:
  feedback: true            # show Feedback buttons (default: true)
  feedback-storage: local   # local | session
  feedback-hints: true      # progressive hints (default: true)
```

::: {.callout-important}
The API key lives in the reader's browser. Never put a key into the `.qmd` — it would be published with the site.
:::

## Options

Per cell:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `context` | `interactive` | `interactive`, `output` or `setup` |
| `read-only` | `false` | editor is locked (no feedback button) |
| `autorun` | — | `true`: run once Pyodide has started |
| `label` | — | unique cell ID |
| `classes` | — | extra CSS classes |
| `fig-cap` | — | caption for plots |
| `fig-width` / `fig-height` | `7` / `5` | plot size in inches |

Per document:

```{.yaml filename="page.qmd"}
pyodide:
  packages: [numpy, pandas]   # installed at startup via micropip
  base-url: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.27.2/
  show-startup-message: true
  lang: de                    # interface language (default: en)
```

Packages that only appear in an `import` are fetched on demand, so `packages:` is for the ones you want ready before the first run. `requests`/`urllib3` are shimmed, so `pd.read_csv(url)` works.

## Install

::: {.callout-important}
## Not yet `quarto add`-able
`pyodide-interaktiv`, `py-exercise` and `math-exercise` are not in the public extension registry yet — only `coatless-quarto/pyodide` is. Until they are published, vendor them by hand.
:::

**① Copy the extension folder**

Copy `_extensions/Erasmus-CTM/pyodide-interaktiv/` from this project into your own project's `_extensions/` folder.

**② Reference it by folder name**

```{.yaml filename="page.qmd"}
---
title: "My Page"
format: html
filters:
  - pyodide-interaktiv
---
```

A vendored extension needs no `quarto add` step, and it is referenced by folder name only — without the `Erasmus-CTM/` prefix that a registry install would add.

::: {.callout-warning}
## One Pyodide extension per page
`coatless-quarto/pyodide` and `pyodide-interaktiv` both claim `{pyodide-python}`. Listing both in `filters:` loads two runtimes and breaks the cells — pick one.
:::

Two more limits worth knowing: `embed-resources` does not work (Pyodide ships WebAssembly binaries), and navigating to another page of the project reloads the runtime.

:::

## py-exercise — editable exercises with hidden tests

**Install:** copy the folder — not published yet\
**Source:** [@py-exercise] — [github.com/Erasmus-CTM/Py-Exercise](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/Py-Exercise)

::: {.callout-note}
## Works on its own
py-exercise no longer needs a Pyodide extension next to it. On its own it loads Pyodide and the Monaco editor from a CDN when the reader first runs an exercise:

```{.yaml filename="exercises.qmd — standalone"}
filters:
  - py-exercise
```

If the page *does* have a Pyodide extension, list it **first** — py-exercise then reuses that runtime instead of booting a second one:

```{.yaml filename="page.qmd — combined"}
filters:
  - pyodide-interaktiv
  - py-exercise
```
:::


::: {.panel-tabset}

## Example

:::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```{py-exercise}
def square(x):
    """Return x squared."""
    # Your solution here
    pass

## TESTS ##
assert square(3) == 9,  "square(3) should be 9"
assert square(0) == 0,  "square(0) should be 0"
assert square(-2) == 4, "square(-2) should be 4"
```
::::

:::: {.content-hidden when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-note}
## Interactive exercise — HTML only
This exercise runs student code in the browser. Render as HTML to try it.
:::
::::

## Syntax

````{.markdown}
```{py-exercise}
def my_function(x):
    """Docstring shown to the reader."""
    # Student fills this in
    pass

## TESTS ##
assert my_function(2) == 4, "Feedback shown on failure"
assert my_function(0) == 0
```
````

Rules:
1. Write the function stub with a docstring at the top.
2. `## TESTS ##` is the separator — everything below is hidden from the reader.
3. Each `assert` statement's message becomes the feedback shown on test failure.

::: {.callout-tip}
Write assertion messages as if you are talking to the student:
`"my_function(2) should return 4 — did you multiply correctly?"`
:::

## Options

Per cell:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | `py-exercise-N` | unique exercise ID |
| `caption` | — | title above the exercise |
| `forbidden-imports` | — | comma-separated imports the solution may not use |
| `forbidden-keywords` | — | comma-separated Python keywords the solution may not use |
| `show-test-hints` | `true` | show the assertion message when a test fails |

Per document — the same keys, applied to every exercise on the page:

```{.yaml filename="exercises.qmd"}
py-exercise:
  forbidden-imports: [os, sys, subprocess]
  forbidden-keywords: [for, while, sorted]
  show-test-hints: true
  lang: de                   # interface language (default: en)
```

## Restricting solutions

Forbidden constructs are checked **before** the code runs — a violation is reported instead of a test result:

````{.markdown}
```{py-exercise}
#| caption: Fibonacci, recursively
#| forbidden-keywords: for, while
def fib(n):
    pass

## TESTS ##
assert fib(6) == 8,   "fib(6) should be 8"
assert fib(10) == 55, "fib(10) should be 55"
```
````

Typical uses: banning `for`/`while` to force recursion or comprehensions, banning `sorted` to make students write the algorithm, banning `os`/`sys`/`subprocess` in an open learning environment.

## Submission

With `submission: true` the page gets a header asking for a student ID and a quiz ID. Once the tests pass, the student can download the result as a JSON file, XOR-encoded with `submission-key` and Base64-wrapped so the raw results are not readable without the key.

```{.yaml filename="exercises.qmd"}
py-exercise:
  submission: true
  submission-key: "sose25-quiz1"
```

::: {.callout-warning}
The key is in the rendered page, so this deters casual tampering — it is not real cryptography. Treat it as a convenience for collecting results, not as an exam-grade safeguard.
:::

:::

## math-exercise — symbolic answers checked with SymPy

**Install:** copy the folder — not published yet\
**Source:** [@math-exercise] — [github.com/Erasmus-CTM/Math-Exercise](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/Math-Exercise)

Where py-exercise checks *code*, math-exercise checks an *answer*. Students type a mathematical expression into an input field and it is compared with SymPy — so any equivalent form counts as correct.

::: {.callout-note}
## Works on its own
Like py-exercise, math-exercise loads Pyodide and SymPy itself on the first **Check** click if no Pyodide extension is present. When one is, list it first:

```{.yaml filename="page.qmd"}
filters:
  - pyodide-interaktiv
  - math-exercise
```
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Example

:::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```{math-exercise}
#| label: exp-circle-area
#| caption: Area of a circle
#| vars: r
A circle has radius $r = 3$. Give its area exactly (use `pi`):

$A =$ _[pi*9]
```
::::

:::: {.content-hidden when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-note}
## Interactive exercise — HTML only
This exercise is checked in the browser with SymPy. Render as HTML to try it.
:::
::::

`pi*9`, `9*pi` and `3**2*pi` are all accepted — they are the same expression.

## Syntax

````{.markdown}
```{math-exercise}
#| label: my-exercise
#| caption: Exercise title
#| vars: x
Question text with an input field: _[correct_answer]
```
````

The answer inside `[...]` is a SymPy expression, e.g. `pi * 9` or `x**2 + 2*x + 1`. Three field widths are available:

| Marker | Width | Element |
|---|---|---|
| `_[answer]` | narrow (~10 characters) | `<input>` |
| `__[answer]` | medium (~20 characters) | `<input>` |
| `___[answer]` | wide, two lines | `<textarea>` |

Several fields in one exercise are checked together on **Check**.

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | `math-exercise-N` | unique exercise ID |
| `caption` | — | title above the exercise |
| `vars` | — | SymPy symbols, e.g. `x, y, r` |
| `mode` | `equivalent` | `equivalent` or `exact` |
| `reject` | — | expression to refuse even though it is correct |
| `pool` | `false` | treat the block as a pool of variants |

```{.yaml filename="page.qmd"}
math-exercise:
  lang: de     # interface language (default: en)
```

::: {.callout-important}
Any symbol used in the answer has to be listed in `vars` — otherwise SymPy has no idea what `x` is meant to be.
:::

## Checking modes

**`equivalent`** *(default)* — accepts every mathematically equivalent form. For `[pi * 9]`, all of `pi*9`, `9*pi` and `3**2 * pi` pass.

**`equivalent` + `reject`** — accepts equivalent forms *except* the one given. This is what makes simplification exercises work: the student cannot just retype the question.

````{.markdown}
```{math-exercise}
#| vars: x
#| mode: equivalent
#| reject: (x+1)**2
Expand: $(x+1)^2 =$ __[x**2 + 2*x + 1]
```
````

→ `(x+1)^2` is refused, `x^2 + 2x + 1` is accepted.

**`exact`** — accepts only SymPy's canonical form of the answer. Use it when one specific notation is required.

## Question pools

With `pool: true` and `---` as a separator, one block holds several variants. Each page visit picks one at random and keeps it for the session; a ↻ button loads a different one.

````{.markdown}
```{math-exercise}
#| label: circle-pool
#| caption: Area of a circle
#| vars: r
#| pool: true
Radius r = 3 cm. $A =$ _[pi*9] cm²

---

Radius r = 5 cm. $A =$ _[pi*25] cm²

---

Radius r = 7 cm. $A =$ _[pi*49] cm²
```
````

All variants share the same options (`vars`, `mode`, `reject`).

## Input help & feedback

Each exercise has a collapsible **input help** listing the notation students need — `x^2` or `x**2`, `sqrt(x)`, `root(x, n)`, `pi`, `E`, `Abs(x)`, `oo`, `integrate(f, x)`, `diff(f, x)`.

The **Feedback** button works like the one in `pyodide-interaktiv`: same settings dialog, same providers, same progressive hint levels — and credentials entered once in `localStorage` are reused across all pages of the project.

:::

## JSXGraph — interactive mathematical graphs

**Install:** `quarto add jsxgraph/jsxgraph`  
**Source:** [@jsxgraph] — [github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto](https://github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto)

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Example

:::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-7, 1.8, 7, -1.8],
    axis: true,
    showNavigation: false
});
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], {
    strokeColor: '#0d6efd', strokeWidth: 2.5
});
var p = board.create('glider', [1.57, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], {
    name: 'x', size: 5, fillColor: '#E91E63'
});
board.create('point', [
    function() { return p.X(); },
    function() { return Math.sin(p.X()); }
], { name: function() { return 'sin(x) ≈ ' + Math.sin(p.X()).toFixed(3); },
     size: 5, fillColor: '#198754', fixed: true });
```
::::

:::: {.content-hidden when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-note}
## Interactive graph — HTML only
This JSXGraph canvas is rendered in the browser. Render as HTML to interact with it.
:::
::::

## Syntax

````{.markdown}
```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5],   // [xmin, ymax, xmax, ymin]
    axis: true,
    keepaspectratio: false,
    showNavigation: false
});
```
````

::: {.callout-important}
Always use the literal string `BOARDID` — Quarto replaces it with a unique ID.
Hardcoding a string breaks pages with multiple graphs.
:::

## Common elements

```{.javascript}
// Function graph
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd' });

// Draggable point
var p = board.create('point', [2, 1], { name: 'P', size: 4 });

// Glider — point constrained to a line/curve
var g = board.create('glider', [1, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], { name: 'x' });

// Slider
var s = board.create('slider', [[0,-3],[4,-3],[0,1,2*Math.PI]], { name: 'a' });

// Use slider value
board.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return Math.sin(s.Value()*x); }]);

// Text label
board.create('text', [1, 2, function() { return 'x = ' + g.X().toFixed(2); }]);

// Segment
board.create('segment', [p1, p2], { strokeColor: '#198754', dash: 2 });
```

:::
